target_customer: Mobile engineering teams and AI coding agents that need to build, run and verify mobile apps; customers shown include Zillow, Tinder, Faire and RevenueCat
problem: Mobile app tests are brittle and slow to maintain, and AI agents cannot verify whether mobile changes work. Revyl started with natural language end-to-end mobile tests and expanded to cloud runtimes and app intelligence.
business_model: B2B SaaS and usage-based cloud runtimes for testing and verification
product_category: mobile testing and development platform for agents

founders.name: Landseer Enga
prior_employers: Web scraping work for PE firms

founders.name: Anam Hira
prior_employers: Uber (software engineering intern 2022, then ML engineer; built DragonCrawl, an LLM-based mobile testing framework)
education: University of British Columbia, computer science and statistics

technical_complexity.rationale: LLM-driven mobile UI testing across iOS and Android with self-healing tests is difficult but the CTO had built a similar internal system at Uber in 2023. Cloud simulators add infrastructure work.

defensibility.rationale: Many AI testing tools (Momentic, QA Wolf, Maestro and others) address the same pain, and a test suite offers moderate lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying documented in sources found.

market_need_then: Uber reported its DragonCrawl LLM mobile tester saved over 25M USD in four months (per BetaKit), showing large spend on mobile QA. Manual and scripted mobile tests were widely seen as flaky.

outcome_analysis: Revyl raised a 1.1M USD pre-seed in September 2024 on the strength of its CTO's Uber DragonCrawl experience and has since broadened into agent verification infrastructure, with well-known app companies listed as customers on its site. No later round is verified, so traction is undocumented beyond company claims. Competition in AI testing is crowded.
